doc.citation: Oktay, B. and Wellman, C.H. (2019). Palynological analysis of Upper Ordovician to Lower Silurian sediments from the Diyarbakir Basin, southeastern Turkey. Review of Palaeobotany and Palynology 263: 28–46.
doc.comment: The complete supplied text reports extremely rare, taxonomically unidentified spores/cryptospores in both formations. These are pooled palynofacies categories, not identified spore taxa. The accompanying accepted-manuscript PDF also lacks the cited tables, figures and plate explanations; their contents could not be checked, so extraction remains provisional. The publisher's highlight says no cryptospores were recovered, conflicting with the body's pooled wording ([publisher page](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0034666718301362)). Steemans, Le Hérissé and Bozdogan (1996), Ordovician and Silurian cryptospores and miospores from southeastern Turkey, is cited for other sections with more common spores; reuse of its material is not stated. Crossref verification was attempted but unavailable.

items.section_or_core: Unnamed studied well in the eastern part of the Diyarbakır Basin
items.age_basis_detail: Chitinozoan assemblages CA1 (late Katian, merga Biozone) and CA2 (cautiously Hirnantian, moussegoudaensis/oulebsiri Biozone), supported by acritarch assemblage AA1. Chitinozoan dating is considered more precise.
items.setting_as_reported: offshore, open marine, shallow shelf that was oxygenated; offshore, open marine, deeper water shelf that was anoxic
items.notes: Marine acritarchs and chitinozoans are the main focus. The lower formation contains extremely rare spores/cryptospores; the upper formation contains very rare spores/cryptospores. These qualitative reports are combined at formation scope because no spore-specific sample distribution is supplied. Sample count represents all selected Upper Ordovician samples, not confirmed spore-positive samples. Cuttings span 1908-2362 m; study-wide core samples span 1826.05-1873.4 m across both formations. Probable reworking concerns acritarchs, and caving introduces Silurian marine palynomorphs into Ordovician cuttings; neither is specifically demonstrated for spores. No spore illustrations occur in the supplied material; missing plates could not be assessed.

items.locality: Diyarbakır Basin, province of Diyarbakır, southeastern Turkey
items.section_or_core: Unnamed studied well in the eastern part of the Diyarbakır Basin
items.age_basis_detail: Chitinozoan assemblage CA3, cautiously assigned to the alargada Biozone, supported by acritarch assemblage AA2. Conochitina cf. alargada and accompanying marine palynomorphs support an Aeronian-Telychian age.
items.setting_as_reported: offshore, open marine, deep basinal environment that was anoxic
items.notes: Marine acritarchs and chitinozoans are the main focus. Spores/cryptospores are reported only as an extremely rare pooled palynofacies category, without taxonomic identifications or sample-specific occurrences. Sample count represents all selected Lower Silurian samples, not confirmed spore-positive samples. CA3 occupies 1826.05-1857.5 m, but spores are not explicitly tied to individual depths. Deposits contain abundant amorphous organic matter and pyrite. No spore-specific reworking is reported. No spore illustrations occur in the supplied material; missing plates could not be assessed.
